title: Limerick’s digital leap: Sustainability through modernization
summary: Constellation’s Limerick plant has generated nuclear power in the community of Pottstown, Pa., northwest of Philadelphia, since the first of two boiling water reactors came on line 40 years ago, in 1986. The plan is to keep Limerick running for at least another 40 years, but from a control room that would look wholly unfamiliar to its 1980s-era operators. Limerick is set to get a major safety-related digital instrumentation and control modernization for its two units, rated at 1,153 MWe and 1,162 MWe, respectively.

title: Navy’s first terrestrial reactor coming to Indiana’s NWS Crane
summary: The Department of Defense has announced the first deployment of a microreactor on a shore-based Navy installation will be at Indiana’s Naval Weapons Station (NWS) Crane and executed jointly with the Army’s Janus Program. Not only will it be a first for the Navy when it is installed by September 2028, it will be Indiana’s first power-producing reactor. Previous announcements regarding advanced reactors on military bases have revolved around the Army and Air Force. Most recently, the Army announced that five reactor developers were selected and paired with five military installations under the Janus Program. Wednesday’s announcement expands the concept into another military branch.

title: Uranium mining ban enacted for New Mexico lands
summary: Garcia Richard On September 4, New Mexico Land Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard issued an executive order that bans the leasing of state lands for new uranium mining and associated activities. The executive order also directs the State Land Office to focus on cleaning up legacy uranium sites and urges the uranium industry and federal government to prioritize legacy uranium problems in the state. According to the State Land Office’s announcement, “New Mexico has a painful history as the largest producer of uranium ore in the United States, which has left a legacy of over 1,000 former uranium mining, milling, and exploratory drilling sites in the state, of which 250 are considered abandoned because they are not associated with a viable responsible party (at least 50 of the sites involve state trust lands).”

title: Entergy protects endangered whooping cranes while increasing reliability for customers
summary: Entergy is partnering with the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries and Fulcrum Air to deploy bird flight diverters on transmission lines across Louisiana, marking a significant milestone in the company’s commitment to protecting the endangered whooping cranes while improving reliability for our customers.
